messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock ordering for Optimize toolkit work: quantization profiles, dynamic batching, and prefix/KV caching. Two customer asks in the pipeline and limited eng capacity. My hypothesis: cache-first for chat-heavy customers, quant-first for embedding-heavy customers, batching as an ops knob. Thoughts?
li: Agree cache looks like the biggest immediate win for chat flows — high reach, relatively low engineering effort. Quantization is higher lift but big for embedding costs.
samira: We should avoid opinions-only. Propose three short spikes (benchmarks + small evals) and then RICE-score results. I can run the quantization spike focusing on embedding pipelines.
jorge: From sales: Customer A explicitly asked for predictable P95 latency and a 20% unit-cost reduction target. Important: caching can change latency variance. Launch criteria need to include P95 SLA checks.
nate: Quick data point — for our top 10 chat customers, prefix reuse is ~40% across sessions. A caching layer could significantly reduce redundant compute. Batching reduces GPU ops but increases tail. We should quantify p95 impact for different batch windows.
maya: Proposed plan: run parallel spikes — caching bench on prod-like traces (3 days), small quant test for embeddings (5 days), and adaptive batching sim in staging (2 days). After spikes, we'll compute RICE and pick an MVP. Who can own each spike?
li: I can own the caching spike. Will instrument traces and run an A/B with synthetic TTLs.
samira: I'll take quant. I'll run quant profiles (8-bit/4-bit where safe), check model quality on eval set.
nate: I'll do the batching simulations — vary batch timeouts and size thresholds, measure throughput vs p95.
maya: Sample RICE scoring template for the post-spike writeup:
```text
R: reach (monthly affected requests)
I: impact (0.25=low, 0.5=med, 1=high)
C: confidence (0-100)
E: effort (person-days)
Score = (R * I * C) / E
```
jorge: Launch criteria (draft): 1) No quality regression vs baseline on eval sets (>95% pass on checks). 2) P95 within customer SLA (<=300ms for targeted chat customers). 3) Cost per 1M tokens reduced >=12% for the measured workload. 4) Rollback plan validated (<30m).
deploy-bot: Reminder — staging experiments touching routing or caches require eng-oncall signoff and a runbook entry.
li: Noted — I'll coordinate with eng-oncall and prepare runbook fragments.
maya: OK — action items captured: li -> caching spike, samira -> quant spike, nate -> batching sims. Reconvene in 6 business days for RICE scoring and decision. Thu 10:00am OK for everyone? :calendar:
jorge: Thu 10 works for me. :thumbsup:
samira: Works.
nate: Works for me.
li: Works.
maya: Great — tagging follow-up: we should include a small customer-facing blurb for sales if caching looks good (basic FAQ + expected cost/latency numbers).
